clue.text: Paint, maybe not Crown, prepared and laid on thick

indicators.note: a crown is the top of something, so removing the crown means dropping the opening letter

blocks.note: a coat of paint is a cover for a wall

explanation.surface: A decorator, using some brand other than Crown, slapped the paint on too heavily.
explanation.walkthrough: Crown is a well-known British paint brand, which makes the surface feel like DIY; here it means the head of the word, its opening letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To overdo something is to exaggerate it, which is what laying it on thick means as an idiom.

clue.text: Getting on with rather unusual student taking out first daughter

indicators.note: taking out the first means the earliest instance of a letter is replaced

explanation.surface: Someone is ageing alongside an odd student who has dropped their eldest daughter.
explanation.walkthrough: The first D of ODDISH is replaced by L.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting on is an idiom for growing old, and oldish means somewhat old.

clue.text: Great exercise raised little energy?

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising something turns it to read upwards

blocks.note: one calorie, 1 cal, a tiny amount of energy

explanation.surface: Was that a hard workout, or did it burn hardly any energy?
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful reading of 'little energy' as 1 CAL, with the digit standing in for I.
explanation.definitionFit: Epical is a variant of epic, meaning grand or heroic in scale.

clue.text: Very latest from McDermid perused from cover to cover

indicators.note: the latest of a word is its final letter

blocks.note: read the whole thing, read fully

explanation.surface: Val McDermid's newest crime novel was devoured from start to finish.
explanation.walkthrough: Val McDermid is a Scottish crime novelist, which makes 'latest' look like her newest book.
explanation.definitionFit: Dreadfully is an informal intensifier, as in dreadfully sorry, meaning very.

clue.text: Butcher's end of year fine overturned

indicators.note: something overturned is turned upside down, so in a down clue it reads the other way

explanation.surface: A butcher closes the year by having a penalty quashed.
explanation.walkthrough: Butcher's is Cockney rhyming slang: butcher's hook for look. Decko is British slang for a look too.
explanation.definitionFit: Both butcher's and decko are British slang for a quick look.

clue.text: Concentrates as opponent turns the air blue in conversation

indicators.note: words heard in conversation are spoken, so we go by how they sound

blocks.note: to turn the air blue is to swear, or cuss

explanation.surface: Someone sharpens their attention while a rival swears freely during a chat.
explanation.walkthrough: Said together, 'foe cusses' sounds just like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Focuses is a verb meaning directs attention closely, the same as concentrates.

clue.text: Pro European celebrities being given titles

blocks.note: pro means in favour of, for

explanation.surface: Pro-European stars are being honoured with titles.
explanation.walkthrough: Titles suggests knighthoods; here 'given titles' is given names.
explanation.definitionFit: Forenames are given names, the titles one is given at birth.

clue.text: Speak seductively to the audience, offering success

indicators.note: an audience hears it, so the sound is what counts

blocks.note: to coo is to murmur softly and lovingly

explanation.surface: A performer woos the crowd with a sultry voice and wins them over.
explanation.walkthrough: The P is silent, as in coup d'etat.
explanation.definitionFit: A coup is a notable success or triumph, as in a publishing coup.

clue.text: Play guitar repetitively, limiting muscle range

indicators.note: limiting means fencing in, so one piece holds the other

blocks.note: strumming is repeatedly brushing the strings
short for pectoral, a chest muscle

explanation.surface: Playing guitar over and over strains the muscles' movement.
explanation.walkthrough: Range looks like range of movement; it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A spectrum is a full range, as in the spectrum of opinion.

clue.text: Team Spurs essentially ousted from just outside the top three depart

indicators.note: the essence of a word is its central letter
ousted from means thrown out, so a letter is removed

blocks.note: a set is a group working together

explanation.surface: A football report: Spurs, kicked out of fourth place, are leaving.
explanation.walkthrough: Spurs is the nickname of Tottenham Hotspur football club. Its U drops out of FOURTH.
explanation.definitionFit: To set forth is to start on a journey, to depart.

clue.text: Vim, number one for rinsing in sink

indicators.note: number one means the leading letter of the following word
one piece is placed in the middle of another word

explanation.surface: Vim is a scouring cleaner, so it reads like a kitchen tip about rinsing in the sink.
explanation.walkthrough: Vim is a British brand of cleaning powder, which sells the kitchen picture; here it means energy.
explanation.definitionFit: Vim and drive both mean energy and determination.

clue.text: Oversized American policeman squeezing in right uniform — time to go without?

indicators.note: squeezing something in means holding it inside

blocks.note: American slang for a police officer
U is Uniform in the NATO alphabet
Lent is the season of fasting and giving things up

explanation.surface: An overweight American policeman forces himself into his uniform and wonders whether it is time to diet.
explanation.walkthrough: Lent is the forty days before Easter when Christians traditionally give something up.
explanation.definitionFit: Corpulent means fat, and oversized describes a person of excessive bulk.

clue.text: Support Kitty taking current approach

indicators.note: taking means taking in, so one piece holds the other

blocks.note: a kitty is a pot of pooled money

explanation.surface: Someone backs a cat that is moving towards an electric current.
explanation.walkthrough: Kitty looks like a cat; it is a shared fund of money. Current looks electrical but means fashionable.
explanation.definitionFit: A standpoint is a point of view, an approach to a question.

clue.text: German guy implicated in nightspot tomfoolery

indicators.note: implicated in means involved within the words that follow

blocks.note: spans the end of nightspot and start of tomfoolery

explanation.surface: A German man is caught up in some silliness at a nightclub.
explanation.definitionFit: Otto is a common German man's name, so a German guy is an example.

clue.text: Old politician supporting current Conservative bugs partner

indicators.note: in a down clue, supporting means sitting underneath, so these pieces come after

explanation.surface: A veteran MP backing a sitting Tory secretly wiretaps a colleague.
explanation.walkthrough: Bugs looks like a verb for wiretapping; it is a plural noun. In a down clue, supporting means placed underneath.
explanation.definitionFit: An accomplice is a partner in crime.

clue.text: Best date, the one holding ultimate appeal?

blocks.note: to court someone is to date them

explanation.surface: The best partner to go out with is the one with the most attraction.
explanation.walkthrough: Ultimate appeal reads as romantic attraction, but it is the last stage of a legal appeal.
explanation.definitionFit: The Supreme Court is the highest court in the land, hearing final legal appeals.

clue.text: Judges middle of free Observer and Spectator

indicators.note: the middle of a word means its central letters

blocks.note: the two central letters of free

explanation.surface: Critics hold sway at the heart of two British papers, The Observer and The Spectator.
explanation.walkthrough: The Observer and The Spectator are British publications, which makes this look like media talk; here they are just people who watch.
explanation.definitionFit: Reviewers judge books, plays and films, giving their verdicts as critics.

clue.text: Attracted to American, cavorted, coming over very forward

indicators.note: attracted to means drawn alongside, so the pieces sit together
something coming over another is covered by it, taken inside

blocks.note: to cavort is to dance about

explanation.surface: Someone smitten with an American dances about and comes across as rather pushy.
explanation.walkthrough: V goes inside DANCED, after A.
explanation.definitionFit: Advanced and forward both describe something ahead of others, as in a forward or advanced pupil.

clue.text: Drink with iron — squash?

blocks.note: to press clothes is to iron them

explanation.surface: A bar order: a drink with iron in it, maybe squash, the fruit cordial.
explanation.walkthrough: Squash seems to be the drink; it is a verb meaning crush. Iron looks like a mineral but is a verb too.
explanation.definitionFit: To suppress a revolt is to squash it, put it down by force.

clue.text: Large drink, spirit perhaps — and what one may get after a few!

definitions.text: what one may get after a few!

blocks.note: a double is a large measure of spirits
a ghostly spirit is one kind of vision or apparition

explanation.surface: Ordering a big measure of spirits leads to blurred sight after a few rounds.
explanation.walkthrough: Spirit seems to be the drink; it is a ghost, a kind of vision.
explanation.definitionFit: Seeing two of everything is a familiar effect of drinking a few too many.

clue.text: Cheap gear, half of college pursuing that!

indicators.note: only half of the word is kept, so the rest is dropped
pursuing means chasing, so this piece comes after

blocks.note: Eton College is a school, and college can mean one

explanation.surface: Tacky equipment, half the college chasing after it!
explanation.walkthrough: Only the first half of the six-letter word for college is used.
explanation.definitionFit: Kitsch is cheap, tasteless art or decoration, in poor taste.

clue.text: Marries a French countess, at last admitting appeal

indicators.note: at last points to the final letter
admitting means letting in, so one piece holds another

explanation.surface: A man weds a French countess, who eventually confesses her charm.
explanation.walkthrough: IT for sex appeal is an old convention, from the film It. IT goes inside UNE plus S.
explanation.definitionFit: To unite two people in marriage is to marry them, as a priest does.

clue.text: Heavy blows, no good for snakes

indicators.note: no here means without, so a letter is taken away

blocks.note: gasps are heavy breaths, blown out hard

explanation.surface: Hard punches are useless against snakes.
explanation.walkthrough: Heavy blows suggests punches; it means panting breaths. Remove G from GASPS.
explanation.definitionFit: Asps are small venomous snakes, Cleopatra's choice.

clue.text: Salvation Army lacking a facility finally opened it up

indicators.note: lacking means without, so some letters must go
finally points to the last letter of the word before
something broken up is in pieces and rearranged

explanation.surface: The Salvation Army, short of premises, finally threw open its doors.
explanation.walkthrough: Salvation Army reads as one name, but Salvation is the definition. ARMY loses A and Y to leave RM, which joins OPENED IT for the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Redemption is deliverance from sin, which is what salvation means in religious language.

clue.text: One who uses evasive words losing wife's support

indicators.note: losing means a letter goes missing

explanation.surface: A slippery talker loses the backing of his wife.
explanation.walkthrough: Weasel words are deliberately vague or evasive.
explanation.definitionFit: An easel is a stand that supports a painting or board.

clue.text: First hint of scrapper's face becoming puffed up

indicators.note: the first hint of a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: A fighter's face swells up after the first punch.
explanation.walkthrough: Puffed up looks like swelling from a blow; it means conceited.
explanation.definitionFit: Smug means self-satisfied, as someone puffed up with pride is.

clue.text: Top cook eats these?

indicators.note: to cook something is to prepare it by changing it, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the cream is the top, the best of anything

explanation.surface: A question about what a leading chef likes to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines: a top chef might well eat these. A cream tea is the English afternoon snack of scones, jam, clotted cream and tea.
explanation.definitionFit: Cream teas are afternoon meals of scones with cream, a treat a cook could make and eat.

clue.text: Little picture books capturing opponents following international

indicators.note: capturing means holding something inside
following means coming after, so the order of the pieces is set

blocks.note: the New Testament, a set of books of the Bible
South and East, opponents at the bridge table

explanation.surface: Picture books in which rival teams from an international match feature.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge, North-South play East-West, so any two adjacent compass points can be opponents.
explanation.definitionFit: An inset is a small picture or map set within a larger one.

clue.text: Mark entertained by some Parisian models

indicators.note: a guest entertained by a host is held inside their home

explanation.surface: A man called Mark is shown a good time by fashion models in Paris.
explanation.walkthrough: Mark looks like a name; it is a sign.
explanation.definitionFit: Designs are patterns or plans, as models are templates to follow.

clue.text: Starter of Lancashire cheese excited those using others' bread?

indicators.note: the starter is the opening letter of the word
excited letters are stirred up and jumbled

explanation.surface: Lancashire cheese, a crumbly English cheese, thrills people eating it on someone else's bread.
explanation.walkthrough: Bread is slang for money, so these are spongers, not sandwich-eaters.
explanation.definitionFit: Leeches are parasites, people who live off the money of others.
